title: Switching, Routing & Wireless Essentials (CCNA 2)
subtitle: Design and secure a switched campus network with redundancy and wireless access
audience_line: Participants who completed CCNA 1 or have equivalent networking experience
overview: This programme is the second of three courses that prepare the Cisco CCNA 200-301 exam, aligned with Cisco Networking Academy Switching, Routing and Wireless Essentials v7. Participants segment networks with VLANs and trunks, route between them, make the LAN resilient with STP, EtherChannel and HSRP, provide addresses with DHCPv4, SLAAC and DHCPv6, secure switch ports against layer 2 attacks, deploy a wireless LAN through a controller secured with WPA2, and compare it with WPA3, and configure and troubleshoot static routing. Every chapter ends with a lab in Cisco Packet Tracer, and the programme closes with a final project: a campus network built and presented by each participant. Enterprise Networking, Security & Automation (CCNA 3) follows.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Participants who completed CCNA 1 or have equivalent networking experience

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Introduction to Networks (CCNA 1), or equivalent: IOS configuration, IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, subnetting. These topics are not taught again

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 42 h: 36 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs on simulated Cisco devices

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant with Cisco Packet Tracer (free with each participant’s Cisco Networking Academy account); physical Cisco switches, routers and a wireless controller for selected labs when the organiser provides a rack; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build a redundant, secured campus LAN with VLANs, inter-VLAN routing, wireless access and static routing, and troubleshoot it

phases.name: Switching & VLANs
phases.focus: Switch configuration, VLANs and trunks, inter-VLAN routing
phases.intro: Participants configure switches for secure remote management, split the network into VLANs carried over 802.1Q trunks, then route between the VLANs with a router-on-a-stick and a layer 3 switch. Validated lab: three VLANs that reach each other through both inter-VLAN routing methods.

chapters.title: Switching Concepts & Configuration
chapters.content: Switch boot and SSH, frame forwarding, collision and broadcast domains

phases.name: Redundancy & Address Services
phases.focus: STP, EtherChannel, DHCPv4, SLAAC and DHCPv6, HSRP
phases.intro: Redundant links and gateways keep a LAN running when one part fails. Participants prevent loops with Rapid PVST+ and bundle links with EtherChannel, hand out IPv4 and IPv6 addresses with DHCPv4, SLAAC and DHCPv6, then protect the default gateway with HSRP. Validated lab: a LAN that keeps forwarding when a link or a gateway fails, with hosts addressed automatically in both IP versions.

chapters.title: STP
chapters.content: Loop prevention, STP and Rapid PVST+, PortFast, BPDU guard

chapters.title: EtherChannel
chapters.content: LACP and PAgP, configuration and verification

phases.name: LAN Security & Wireless
phases.focus: Layer 2 attack mitigation, WLAN with a controller, WPA2 and WPA3
phases.intro: Participants protect switch ports against common layer 2 attacks, then deploy a wireless LAN managed by a wireless LAN controller and secured with WPA2 and WPA3. Validated lab: a switch that blocks a rogue DHCP server with DHCP snooping and shuts down a port on a port-security violation, and a WLAN configured on the controller with WPA2-Personal and WPA2-Enterprise.

chapters.title: LAN Security
chapters.content: Port security, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, VLAN and STP attack mitigation

chapters.title: Wireless LANs
chapters.content: 802.11 concepts, WLAN components, WLC configuration, WPA2 and WPA3

phases.name: Routing
phases.focus: Routing table, static and default routes, troubleshooting, skills integration
phases.intro: Participants read the routing table and configure IPv4 and IPv6 static, default and floating static routes, troubleshoot them methodically, then combine switching, routing and wireless in one integration lab. Validated lab: two sites joined by IPv4 and IPv6 static routes, with a floating static route that takes over when the primary link fails, inside the integrated switching and wireless topology.

chapters.title: Routing Concepts & Static Routing
chapters.content: Routing table, path selection, IPv4 and IPv6 static, default and floating static routes

chapters.title: Troubleshooting Static Routes
chapters.content: Methodical troubleshooting of static and default routes

chapters.title: Skills Integration
chapters.content: Integrated switching, routing and wireless lab

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A campus network, built and presented
phases.intro: Each participant builds a campus network in Packet Tracer from a written brief, reusing the phase labs, then documents it and defends the design in front of the group.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, then build VLANs and trunks, inter-VLAN routing, STP and EtherChannel, HSRP and static routing

chapters.title: Services, Security & Documentation
chapters.content: DHCPv4 and DHCPv6, LAN security, the WLAN; topology diagram and addressing table

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Failover demo (link and gateway), questions and feedback

project.title: Campus Network
project.brief: A campus network with VLANs and trunks, inter-VLAN routing, STP and EtherChannel, HSRP, DHCPv4 and DHCPv6, LAN security, a controller-based WLAN and static routing to the provider, which keeps working when a link or gateway fails.
project.stack: Cisco Packet Tracer, Cisco IOS switches and routers, wireless LAN controller, IPv4, IPv6
project.deliverable: Packet Tracer file, topology diagram, addressing table, failover demo
